The "How the Advisors Are Built" section is the real lesson. The roast only lands because each persona is grounded in how that person actually decides — Wickman asks who owns the issue, Buffett asks what the downside is. Skip that grounding and you get generic advice with famous names pasted on. It's the same rule in the systems I build for business owners: an agent's output is capped by the judgment you encode into it upfront. The debate format just makes the trade-offs visible instead of averaging them into mush.

What I find tricky with this process is that, no matter how you get to a decision, the human will only apply it when they agree with it. If the roast room agent tells you to sell your house and all-in spacex stock, will you do it? The lacking piece is rarely how to make AI arrives a smart decision, you know it's LLM behind the scene and they are not responsible to anything they say. And that's why you can't build trust, thus it doesn't matter the decision comes from a roast-room or gpt-3.5
